core_obligations: Part (1): the two fibres of W are effective Cartier divisors because the generic point of W is not mapped into either standard section of the projective line, by the pullback criterion for effective Cartier divisors (proof lines 3362-3367).

Part (2): the closed immersions of the two standard sections into the projective line make W_0 and W_infty isomorphic to closed subschemes of X, the projection W -> X is proper as a composite of a closed immersion and the proper projection, and the graph lemma gives the rational equivalence of the two fibre classes on W; pushing forward along the proper projection gives the same equivalence on X (proof lines 3369-3378).
Part (3): given parts (1) and (2) the only remaining content is that the collection of the two fibres of a locally finite family W_i is locally finite in X, which is clear (proof lines 3380-3383).

Part (4): write a rationally trivial cycle alpha as a locally finite sum of pushforwards of divisors of rational functions f_i on integral V_i of dimension k + 1, and for each i take W_i to be the closure of the graph of f_i inside V_i times the projective line; the same graph lemma identifies the pushed forward divisor with the difference of the two fibre classes, which exhibits alpha in the required form (proof lines 3385-3400).
proof_roadmap: Effective Cartier property of the two fibres from the generic point of W (proof lines 3362-3367).
Rational equivalence of the two fibre classes on W and, by proper pushforward, on X (proof lines 3369-3378).
Local finiteness of the family of fibres (proof lines 3380-3383).
Generation of a rationally trivial cycle: take the closure of the graph of each rational function and read the divisor off the two fibre classes (proof lines 3385-3400).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the technical engine behind the identification of rational equivalence with the relations coming from the projective line: it shows that for an integral W in the product of X with the projective line, not equal to either standard fibre, the two fibres are effective Cartier divisors that can be viewed in X and are rationally equivalent, that the same holds for a locally finite family, and conversely that every rationally trivial cycle arises this way (statement lines 3334-3360, tag 02S4). The proof combines the pullback criterion for effective Cartier divisors, the properness of the projection, the graph construction attached to a rational function and the proper pushforward statement for rational equivalence, and the last part requires building the W_i from the rational functions realising the triviality of alpha. That construction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
